title: GRADUATION CEREMONIES
full_story:
Area Colleges, High schools, and Jr. Highs are gearing up for their graduation ceremonies.

The Clay City High School will have their graduation tonight at 7 pm in the new Gym.  The Clay City 8th Grade Graduation will be held on Tuesday, at 7 pm in the new gym.

Cisne Middle Schools graduation will be held tonight at 6 pm in the Middle School Gym and the High School graduation will be at tomorrow at 2 pm in the High School Gym.

Flora High School Graduation is scheduled for Sunday, May 10th at 2 pm at Conley Gym.  Floyd Henson JR. High Graduation will be held on Thursday, May 21st at 7 pm in the Larry McGrew Gymnasium.

Full Armor Christian Academy is having their JR High and High School graduation ceremonies on Friday, May 15th.  The JR High Graduation will be at 5 pm and the High School Graduation will be at 7 pm in the Open Air Chappel.

North Clay is having High School graduation and baccalaureate on Sunday, May 17th with the Baccalaureate at 2 pm and Graduation at 3 pm at the CCSB Arena.  The JR High Graduation will be held on May 18th at 6:30 pm in the CCSB Arena.

Olney Central College will hold its 62nd annual graduation on Friday, May 15th at 6 pm in the OCC Gymnasium.  Friends and relatives of the graduates are invited to attend.

And, Frontier Community College will also have their 48th annual Commencement ceremonies on Friday, May 15th at 7 pm in the Fairfield Community High School Gym.

title: ELMWOOD CEMETERY CLEANUP
full_story:
In order to prepare Elmwood Cemetery for Memorial Day, The City of Flora and Elmwood Cemetery personnel request that all floral arrangements and old decorations that are on the ground, including grave blankets, be removed from all graves prior to Monday, May 18th.  This request does not include floral arrangements that are in the monument vases , or hanging floral arrangements. All ground floral arrangements and old decorations left on graves after May 18th, will be removed by cemetery personnel.

The City and Elmwood Cemetery personnel thank you for your cooperation.

title: AMERICAN LEGION WALK TOMORROW
full_story:
The Flora and Louisville American Legions will be sponsoring the 3rd annual “Be The One” walk to raise public awareness to Veteran’s suicide tomorrow morning.

The walk will start at 8 am at the Clay County World War 2 Memorial across from the Flora VFW, and end at the Clay County Veterans Monument on the Clay County Courthouse Square.  The walk will be followed by a lunch provided by the Louisville American Legion and transportation will be provided back to Flora.  Everyone is invited to attend.

Last year’s walk had 125 walkers and raised $15,000 for the cause and they hope to top that effort this year, with a goal of 250 walkers.  For more information or to register call or stop by either of the American Legion Posts.

title: STAMP OUT HUNGER
full_story:
Tomorrow marks the 34th anniversary of the National Association of Letter Carriers Stamp Out Hunger Food Drive.

Each year, letter carriers across the country head out on their routes on the second Saturday in May to collect donations of non-perishable food items to benefit local food pantries.  Since launching in 1993, the National Association of Letter Carriers’ annual Stamp Out Hunger Food Drive has grown into the nation’s largest one-day food drive, helping to fill the shelves of food banks in cities and towns throughout the United States.

The need is great, but you can help.  Post Office’s in Clay County are inviting you to join letter carriers and their partner organizations in the fight to end hunger in our communities by participating in the annual Stamp Out Hunger Food Drive.  Simply leave your donation of non-perishable food in a bag near your mailbox on Saturday, and your letter carrier will do the rest.  Participation is voluntary.

Currently more than 44 million Americans are unsure where their next meal will come from.  More than 13 million are children and more than 5.5 million seniors over the age of 60 are food insecure.

title: SALEM POLICE CHIEF
full_story:
Salem City Manager Lisa Peck announced the appointment of Tyler Rose as the next Chief of Police for the Salem Police Department.  The appointment takes effect immediately.

Peck says Chief Rose brings nearly a decade of experience with the Salem Police Department, most recently serving as Deputy Chief since January 2025.  During his tenure, he has held several specialized assignments, including service with the Child Death Investigation Task Force, the South Central Illinois Special Response Team, and Internal Affairs.  He has participated in SWAT operations and holds multiple instructor certifications in defensive tactics, arrest and control techniques, and use-of-force training.  His credentials include certifications in PPCT, Integrated Force Options, L.O.C.K.U.P., and de-escalation strategies.

Peck says throughout his career, Chief Rose has demonstrated a strong commitment to public safety, professionalism, and community-oriented policing.  He graduated summa cum laude from Southern Illinois University Edwardsville with a Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice.  Rose is also a recent graduate of the Northwestern Center for Public Safety’s School of Police Staff and Command, a nationally recognized leadership and management program for law enforcement professionals.

title: CARLE RICHLAND TO EXPAND
full_story:
The Carle Health system board approved a $45 million investment in Carle Richland Memorial Hospital, including a new specialty medical office building and an expansion of the Emergency Department (ED), located in Olney.  The effort is part of Carle Health’s continued commitment in bringing access to high-quality care and services across the region.

By bringing specialty services together and expanding the Emergency Department, this investment improves coordination for care teams and helps patients access timely care more easily, close to home.  The new facility will consolidate outpatient specialty clinics currently located in Carle Richland Memorial Hospital, as well as additional locations at Carle Surgical Services and Carle Olney.  It will also house a new laboratory space and infusion center for the community.

Gina Thomas, president of Carle Richland Memorial Hospital, is pleased to share the news with the community about the major additions and updates they will notice taking place soon.

“Carle Richland has been a part of this community for over 70 years and we have been putting a lot of work and effort into our campus planning for the future,” Thomas said.  “This specialty medical office building will bring all of our outpatient specialty services, such as cardiology, urology, podiatry, just to name a few, to one location.  Above all, this positions us for growth and expansion opportunities to provide additional specialty services as we look at what’s most needed ahead.”

The 46,000 square foot, two-story clinic will be built on the southwest side of the current Carle Richland Memorial Hospital campus.  It will attach to the hospital, making movement between the hospital and clinic easy for both team members and patients.

The medical office building is set to break ground late summer.  Upon the completion of the medical office building, projected in late Fall of 2027, work will begin on the expansion of the Carle Richland Emergency Department.

“This is a two-phased building project,” Thomas said.  “By moving the Laboratory into the new building, we will be able to expand the Emergency Department and make dedicated areas for registration, triage and private patient care rooms.  With these changes patients can continue to count on safe, high-quality care from local, compassionate care teams at the Carle Richland medical campus”

The Emergency Department expansion project will begin in the fall of 2027, with a target completion date of summer 2028.

title: AMY CENTER GRANT
full_story:
The Amy Schultz Child Advocacy Center received a $210,000 three-year grant to provide mental health services.

Executive Director Michaele Wharton says in the past the services had to be outsourced and were not immediately available.

“That will help us increase our services,” Wharton said.  “In 36 years, we’ve never been able to have an in-house therapist.  It will just allow us to be able to offer more holistic services all around.  We’ve been able to refer out for mental health, which has been wonderful and we have some great partners, but we’ve always dreamed of being able to offer that as one of our core and direct services within the Amy Center.  That will make something that has never been a reality a possibility for us through the St. Clare Foundation.”

Wharton says the case load of sexual assault and abuse cases remains high in their seven-county service area that includes Marion, Jefferson, Washington, Wayne, Hamilton, and Clay.

“The cases are manageable,” Wharton said.  “I will say the new intakes are going up, but the case load is remaining manageable because of the partnership with our multidisciplinary teams.  Because we’re meeting so frequently and having important discussions with those team members like law enforcement, prosecution, and child protection, we’re able to service a lot of cases in a more timely fashion than what used to be the case.”

Wharton says the grant is coming from the St. Clare Foundation, which is making grants available to several area non-profit groups and schools to help address mental health issues.  She notes the Amy Center is currently advertising for the mental health professional to fill the position.

title: GAS TAX INCREASE
full_story:
Illinois drivers will see another gas tax increase on July 1st.

The state tax will rise to 49.6 cents per gallon because of the automatic annual inflation increase built into the 2019 “Rebuild Illinois” infrastructure program signed by Governor J.B. Pritzker.

That means Illinois drivers will continue paying among the highest gas taxes in the country.  Indiana and Georgia gave residents a gas tax holiday from high prices because of the war in Iran.

The average price of a gallon of gas in Illinois was $4.986 on May 6th, up from about $3.40 a year ago, according to the AAA.

When Pritzker doubled the state gas tax from 19 cents to 38 cents in 2019, lawmakers also ensured Illinoisans would face automatic inflation-linked increases every year without another recorded vote.

Once federal, state and local taxes are combined, many Illinois drivers pay more than 85 cents per gallon in taxes alone at the pump.  Only California and Michigan rival Illinois for the highest total gas taxes in the country.

For the average driver, those increases add up fast.  Illinois motorists now pay nearly $150 more annually in state gas taxes than they did before the 2019 increase.

Drivers in Cook, DuPage, Kane, Lake, McHenry and several other counties pay even more because of additional local gas taxes.
